Enter IP addresses that are not in the config, one per line (commas and spaces work too), at most 20. Resolve domains to IPv4 in the separate domain field below, select the results; putting them in this box replaces its existing contents; do not enter domains directly here. Direct latency testing still uses the domain in the page-top field as SNI and Host. Via-node latency testing temporarily replaces the selected node server with the IP in this box. The test also reads the ingress data centre, registered operator and registered location; direct mode also tests ports and ECH. The two download URLs are used only after testing, when you tap Download on a table row; neither latency-test button uses them. Every IP is tried 10 times (up to 5 at once, each at most 3 seconds).
Ports (direct latency test: each working IP gets a handshake on these ports, separated by spaces or commas)
Direct download-test URL (for download testing only; direct; must be hosted on Cloudflare)
Via-node download-test URL (for download testing only; through the node; preferably not hosted on Cloudflare — Workers can be slow to access CF sites and may time out)

Tap an IP to copy it; tap a ports cell for port results; Download applies to that row only (up to 10 MB or 5 seconds from the first byte); ingress DC* in via-node mode is read using one extra direct connection; the table scrolls sideways, Speed is at the far right. In detailed diagnostics, - means no response, None means the item is absent, and Not obtained means an expected value was not read. Certificates are not verified because the core cannot read Android\'s system certificate store. In via-node tests, Exit IP is the address seen by the target site; it is different from the registered operator of the entry IP.
A port that fails may be the IP, or your ISP blocking that port.
No port results for this row (the IP itself failed, or via-node mode)

Target URL (used for via-node latency and exit data centre; optional. To see the exit data centre, use a Cloudflare-hosted site)
The target address must start with http:// or https://

Latency and failure rate are measured by requesting the target URL through the node. Site reaction is its response; Exit data centre is read from its Cf-Ray header. The target must be hosted on Cloudflare to provide an exit data centre. The target URL is used for latency and exit data-centre checks; leaving it blank keeps the existing behavior.
%1$s target page moves the browser on by itself (meta refresh or script) to: %2$s

Handshake latency = TCP connection + TLS handshake. Jitter is the mean deviation of successful results from their average.

Via-node latency = total time for a request through the node to the target URL; if blank, the node\'s built-in test URL is used. Ingress DC* is read using one extra direct connection; via-node mode does not test ports, so the port column shows “-”. Exit country is the country of the exit IP; exit data centre is the receiving data centre read from the target site’s response. They come from different locations and need not match. Use exit country when judging whether the target site is reachable. Jitter is the mean deviation of successful results from their average.
